key_insight: BRIDGE replaces frequent data-qubit shuttling with a static buffer-relay fabric and a lazy-move compiler, preserving connectivity while reducing motion-induced errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
engineering_relevance: This enables more scalable and lower-loss compilation for dual-species neutral-atom hardware by using compiler-managed buffer atoms to route interactions without moving the data atoms in most cases.
method: Static 2D interleaved dual-species array with non-encoding buffer atoms
Calibrated heteronuclear and homonuclear Rydberg interactions form a routing backbone
Lazy-move compiler limits data motion to selected hotspots instead of broad transport
evidence_signal: Across 22 benchmark circuits under a shared error model, BRIDGE reports about 10× higher geometric-mean fidelity than ZAP and 16× than Enola, while also cutting execution time by roughly 540× and 1000×, respectively.
watch_item: The approach depends on precise calibration and reliable control of dual-species interactions, so hardware complexity and sensitivity to crosstalk or species-specific errors may affect practical deployment.
paper_title: Lazy-Move Compilation for Neutral-Atom Quantum Computers via a Buffer-Relay Fabric
